newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Former Ethiopia military junta accused of genocide.
newsitem.headline: Former Ethiopia military junta accused of genocide.

text.p: A prosecution witness at the trial of Ethiopia's former "Dergue" Marxist military rulers accused them on Tuesday of trying to exterminate the Tigrayan people.

"The former government of Mengistu Haile Mariam, known as the Dergue, conducted an act of genocide against the Tigrayan ethnic group similar to the Nazi persecution of the Jews," a former government official told a court in Addis Ababa.
"The Dergue may have had no written policy to exterminate the Tigray ethnic group, but I have seen it in action, when hundreds of thousands were being annihilated without reason."

The 56-year-old witness, who under court rules cannot be named, said he was tortured for more than five years during the military junta's 17 years in power because he was a Tigrayan. He accused the Dergue of rounding up people of Tigrayan origin and executing them without reason.
He was testifying at the trial of 71 former Dergue officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity. They face the death penalty if found guilty.
Only 46 of the 71 accused are in court. The others, including Mengistu Haile Mariam who ruled Ethiopia from 1977 to 1991 and now lives in Zaimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.

The witness, a brother of a top Ethiopian rebel leader, said he was taken from his office in 1984 to a torture centre. He said he was tortured to force him to admit being in the Tigray People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (TPLF).
"I was blindfolded, hung upside down, beaten continuously and subjected to electric shocks for a number of days and nights," said the witness. He was repeatedly submerged in filthy water.
The trial was adjourned until Thursday. Prosecutors have charged 5,198 people with war crimes, aggravated homicide and genocide under the Dergue.
